key_insight: EVENET learns reusable patterns from simulated particle collisions, then transfers that knowledge to multiple analysis tasks. It also works on real collider data, connecting simulation-based training with experimental analysis.
problem_solved: Particle collision analysis needs models that can support different tasks and remain useful when moving from simulated collisions to real experimental data.
method: Pretrain a foundation model, EVENET, on simulated particle collision data.
Combine self-supervised learning with training guided by physics labels.
Transfer the pretrained model across analysis tasks and apply it to real collider data.
impact: EVENET demonstrates how foundation-model training can support scientific data analysis beyond language and images. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights the potential of combining self-supervision with domain-specific labels to build transferable models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: simulated collisions → EVENET pretraining → multiple analysis tasks.
Two training inputs merging into EVENET: self-supervised learning and physics labels.
Simulation-to-experiment bridge linking synthetic collision events with real collider data.
Hub-and-spoke graphic showing one pretrained model supporting several downstream analyses.
paper_title: Foundation model for particle collision data analysis
paper_authors: Ting-Hsiang Hsu, Baihong Zhou, Qibin Liu, Yue Xu, Shu Li
